top_choice_rationale: P001 credits Katori and Ye for the invention and realisation of optical lattice clocks. The magic-wavelength lattice is a distinct physical idea: it cancels the light shift of the clock transition while holding many neutral atoms in the Lamb-Dicke regime, trading single-ion projection-noise limits for ensemble statistics and opening the 10^-18 regime. The result is mature and independently reproduced, and the citation scoped to invention and realisation answers the overlap objection with the 2005 and 2012 prizes. The omission of Lemonde, Takamoto, Lisdat and others is the ordinary cost of the three-person limit. This is a sound achievement, so I rank it above no award.
